R057-01.notes: Narrator (14) helps Halvorsen, who is moving away, plant bulbs; final paragraph says 'By then I thought I knew' why. B: house already sold in August; narrator persuades no one. C: the garden blooms exactly as arranged, not poor. D: fences are only background ('had built half the fences'); the teaching is about bulbs.

R057-02.notes: White bulbs placed where 'they would surprise people'; new family finds them in April, mother reacts as if she'd been left a message. A: house was sold in August, before the planting, so price can't be the motive. B: no future job mentioned. D: narrator says they won't come up until April, after the Nov 1 move.

R057-03.notes: Adult narrator gently mocks the 14-year-old's belief that stating the obvious was helpful, which shows youthful lack of understanding in hindsight. A: the line is about the narrator, not Halvorsen's failure to explain. C: overstates; mild self-irony, not rudeness, and Halvorsen answers 'That's right' calmly. D: no gardening career mentioned.

R057-04.notes: Directly stated: 'three times its own height.' A: red were near the steps, yellow by the mailbox. B: the passage says which end to point 'toward the sky'; nothing about facing the ground. C: arranged in color groups with whites scattered, not a single line.

R057-05.notes: 'because that seemed like the polite thing to do' means the narrator respects a private moment. B: no boredom shown, and they work until the light fades. C: no disapproval stated. D: the stated reason is politeness, not concentration.

R057-06.notes: 'Sleeping' bulbs under the tricycle path, and the narrator 'said nothing to anyone', so the gift stays hidden from the family all winter. A: the tulips 'came up exactly as he had arranged them', so no damage. B: no dislike shown. D: whites were deliberately scattered by Halvorsen, not moved by the tricycle.

flags.note: 'Watery' (D) is a recognized idiom for pale, weak light ('watery light/sun'), so a strong reader could find it partly defensible. 'Faint' is clearly better because it captures fading dusk light, so a single best answer still holds. Consider replacing D with a less light-associated word (e.g., 'sparse' or 'diluted').

R057-07.notes: 'Worked until the light went thin' at dusk means the light grew faint/dim. A and C (narrow, slender) are physical-width senses that don't apply to light. D: see flag.

R057-08.notes: 'As if someone had left her a message she was still working out how to read' means she senses the deliberate arrangement was meant for someone to find. B: the tricycle isn't mentioned in that scene and she is turning to look at the flowers. C: 'as if' signals a figurative message; the narrator writes to Halvorsen, not Halvorsen to her. D: no disapproval.

flags.note: D nearly copies the passage's last clause ('come out smaller than it was'), so it can be matched without interpretation. Also, in the passage 'it' refers to the reason, while D says 'the gesture'. That reading is defensible, but the key slightly reframes the text. A light paraphrase (e.g., 'reduced the meaning of what he had done') would test comprehension better.

R057-09.notes: Final sentence: writing the reason down 'would come out smaller than it was.' A: daughter not involved. B: the narrator 'thought I knew' and doesn't doubt the guess. C: not suggested.

flags.note: The wording 'a neighbor recalling a time when the narrator was fourteen' is awkward because the neighbor IS the narrator, yet the choice refers to the narrator in third person as if a different person. Suggest 'a neighbor recalling events from when he or she was fourteen.'

R057-10.notes: First person 'I', 'our street', 'from my window', 'I was fourteen' (past/retrospective). A: Halvorsen never explains, and the 'I' isn't him. B: the mother is seen from outside. D: first person, limited, does not know others' thoughts.

R057-11.notes: 'A male who sees a flash at the wrong interval is likely to keep flying.' B/D: brightness is never discussed. C: females perch below as a matter of course, which is the normal exchange and not a reason to keep flying.
